source.title_on_document: Who Is the Best Helper for University Students' Mathematical Creativity? A Quasi-Experimental Study of Human-ChatGPT, Human-Google, and Human-Human Co-Creation

supplement.where: Wiley online Supporting Information ('Appendix. Supporting document.'), p. 16
supplement.holds: Appendix Tables A1 and A3 (correlations between self-evaluation, perceived usefulness, self-efficacy and actual performance) and the MCT scoring reference tables (p. 6, p. 11, p. 12). The main creativity statistics (Table 3) are in the main text.

paper_design_summary: 230 Chinese university students were assigned by lottery to solve a four-task mathematical creativity test (MCT) with ChatGPT (n = 60), with Google Search (n = 60), or in human-human dyads (110 students, 55 dyads), after first solving a baseline task alone. Solutions were scored by two scorers for flexibility, fluency, and originality (rarity of answer categories). Questionnaires measured self-evaluation, interest, difficulty, effort, partner usefulness, and creative self-efficacy.

studies.label: Mathematical creativity task with ChatGPT, Google Search, or a human peer

assignment.what_was_assigned: Co-creation partner: ChatGPT, Google Search, or a human peer (dyad)
assignment.quote: Each student was randomly assigned to one of the three experimental conditions (human-ChatGPT group, human-Google group, or human-human group) using a lottery system.

arms.name: Human-ChatGPT
arms.description: Student solves the MCT with ChatGPT open in one browser tab on a lab computer; free to use the browser but no one searched.

arms.name: Human-Google
arms.description: Student solves the MCT with Google Search only; other AI tools and search engines blocked.

arms.name: Human-Human
arms.description: Student pairs; person A leads and person B plays a supportive, passive role without working independently.

participants.exclusions: None: 'Each participant completed all the required tasks, and none were excluded' (p. 3). The paper gives no count at the moment of assignment. The human-human arm is 110 students in 55 dyads; the ANOVA degrees of freedom F(2, 172) and t(54) for that group are consistent with 175 analysis units (60 + 60 + 55), so the dyad may be the unit for that arm, but the paper does not say so.
participants.who: Chinese university students from all majors (sciences, liberal arts, engineering), mean age about 19, volunteers rewarded with course credits
participants.quote: A total of 230 Chinese university students participated in this study. ... the human-ChatGPT group contained 60 participants, the human-Google group contained 60 participants, and the human-human group contained 110 participants (55 dyads).

ai_tool.how_used: ChatGPT opened in a single browser tab; students were told it could answer prompts, could be given background, could be asked to refine responses, and could take uploaded images or documents. Participants were 'encouraged to draw inspiration from their partner'.

task.description: Mathematical creativity tasks adapted from Lee and Seo: four open-ended geometry tasks asking for as many solutions as possible (2 cm^2 figures on a 4x4 grid, methods to measure dispersion of marbles, properties of water in a tilted prism, shared features of geometric shapes). A baseline number-pyramid task was solved alone beforehand.
task.duration: Whole study 80 min (SD 7) in human-ChatGPT, 70 min (SD 5) in human-Google, 68 min (SD 7.8) in human-human (p. 3)

outcomes.name: MCT originality
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Two scorers marked answers correct, categorized them, and scored each category's rarity: 3, 2, or 1 point if its share of all responses fell in (0,1%], (1%,2%], (2%,3%]; summed over four tasks. Cohen's kappa above 0.91. Mixed ANOVA on z-standardized scores (baseline vs MCT) also reported; ANCOVA with prior math competence as covariate.

contrasts.reported: Human-ChatGPT M = 5.47 (SD 2.83), Human-Google M = 3.88 (SD 2.32), Human-human M = 7.00 (SD 3.10); omnibus F(2, 172) = 18.31, eta_p^2 = 0.18, p < 0.001 (Bonferroni-corrected). Mixed ANOVA: condition F(2, 172) = 8.56, eta_p^2 = 0.09, p < 0.001; interaction F(2, 172) = 8.19, eta_p^2 = 0.09, p < 0.001. Within-group change baseline to MCT: ChatGPT t(59) = 0.12, p = 0.906, d = 0.02; Google t(59) = 3.14, p < 0.010, d = 0.48 (decrease). No pairwise between-arm test printed.
contrasts.locator: p. 7, Table 3 row 4; pp. 7-8, Section 6.1; p. 8, Figure 2

contrasts.reported: Human-ChatGPT M = 5.47 (SD 2.83, N = 60) vs Human-human M = 7.00 (SD 3.10, N = 110 students / 55 dyads); omnibus F(2, 172) = 18.31, eta_p^2 = 0.18, p < 0.001. Human-human within-group increase t(54) = 2.73, p < 0.010, d = 0.45. Text: 'the human-human group achieved greater originality than the other groups'. No pairwise between-arm test printed.

outcomes.name: MCT flexibility
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Number of correct answer categories in each task, summed over four tasks; same scorers. Mixed ANOVA on z-standardized scores and ANCOVA also reported.

contrasts.reported: Human-ChatGPT M = 15.03 (SD 3.78), Human-Google M = 12.83 (SD 3.29), Human-human M = 12.38 (SD 3.35); omnibus F(2, 172) = 9.71, eta_p^2 = 0.10, p < 0.001. Mixed ANOVA: condition F(2, 172) = 3.80, eta_p^2 = 0.04, p < 0.05; interaction F(2, 172) = 6.08, eta_p^2 = 0.07, p < 0.01. Within-group change: ChatGPT t(59) = 2.48, p < 0.050, d = 0.44; Google t(59) = 0.71, p = 0.483, d = 0.11.

Human-ChatGPT M = 15.03 (SD 3.78) vs Human-human M = 12.38 (SD 3.35); omnibus F(2, 172) = 9.71, p < 0.001. Human-human within-group change t(54) = 2.24, p < 0.050, d = 0.36. No pairwise between-arm test printed.

outcomes.name: MCT fluency
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Number of correct answers in each category (maximum five per category), summed over four tasks. Mixed ANOVA on z-standardized scores and ANCOVA also reported.

contrasts.reported: Human-ChatGPT M = 27.85 (SD 7.56), Human-Google M = 23.78 (SD 6.50), Human-human M = 23.42 (SD 5.93); omnibus F(2, 172) = 7.91, eta_p^2 = 0.08, p = 0.001. Mixed ANOVA: condition F(2, 172) = 3.31, eta_p^2 = 0.04, p < 0.05; interaction F(2, 172) = 4.68, eta_p^2 = 0.05, p < 0.05. Within-group change: ChatGPT t(59) = 2.14, p < 0.050, d = 0.39; Google t(59) = 0.80, p = 0.426, d = 0.13.

Human-ChatGPT M = 27.85 (SD 7.56) vs Human-human M = 23.42 (SD 5.93); omnibus F(2, 172) = 7.91, p = 0.001. Human-human within-group change t(54) = 1.90, p = 0.064, d = 0.31. No pairwise between-arm test printed.

eligibility.reason: The Methods state that each student was randomly assigned by lottery to ChatGPT, Google Search, or a human peer (p. 3), 230 students were analyzed with none excluded (60 ChatGPT, 60 Google, 110 in dyads), and flexibility, fluency, and originality are scored on the solutions by two scorers (pp. 6-7). The title and the limitations section call the design quasi-experimental and suggest matching for comparable groups (p. 12), and the 60/60/110 split is uneven for an equal-chance lottery, so the reviewer should confirm criterion 1. The comparison groups are other aids (Google, a human peer), not no help.

one_line_finding: Students working with ChatGPT scored higher on flexibility (15.03 vs 12.83 Google, 12.38 peer) and fluency (27.85 vs 23.78, 23.42) of math-creativity solutions, while peer dyads scored highest on originality (7.00 vs 5.47 ChatGPT, 3.88 Google) (p. 7, Table 3).
open_questions: The title says 'Quasi-Experimental Study' and the limitations (p. 12) recommend 'advanced matching techniques to create more comparable groups', yet Section 3.1 says each student was randomly assigned by lottery with equal chance. Is this a randomized experiment?
Arm sizes 60/60/110 are uneven under an equal-chance lottery; the paper does not explain how dyads were formed or why the human-human arm is larger.

Analysis degrees of freedom (F(2, 172), t(54) for human-human) imply 175 units, so the human-human arm seems to be analyzed as 55 dyads or one member per dyad; Table 3 does not state the unit for that group.
No pairwise between-arm tests are printed for flexibility, fluency, or originality; only the omnibus F and within-group baseline-to-MCT changes. Table 3 p-values are Bonferroni-corrected.
The baseline task (number pyramid) differs from the MCT tasks, so the within-group baseline-to-MCT changes compare different tests on z-scores.
notes: Outcomes left out because they are self-reported, not scored on output: self-evaluation of flexibility, fluency, and originality; bias index (self-evaluation minus percentile-based actual score); interest; difficulty; mental effort; partner usefulness; own and partner contribution; creative self-efficacy pre and post (Table 3 rows 5-18). Table 3 row 1 (creativity baseline, solved alone before assignment took effect): ChatGPT 15.53 (5.70), Google 15.15 (6.48), human 15.91 (6.51), F = 0.21, p = 0.808. The ChatGPT-versus-human-peer contrast is coded ai_vs_active per the codebook (a human partner is another aid). ANCOVA: prior math competence unrelated to flexibility, fluency, originality (p. 8).
